diagnostic_attribution_rules.retrieval_omission: A required mapped surface exists before cutoff but is absent from the retrieved/context packet.
diagnostic_attribution_rules.formation_omission: A required mapped surface is available to formation, but the expected State/Fact/Relation proposal is absent or wrong.
diagnostic_attribution_rules.answer_model_failure: Required mapped surfaces are present in the answer input, and required formed artifacts are present where the condition uses them, but the answer still violates the oracle.

failure_families.name: False promotion
failure_families.definition: Noise, brainstorming, rumor, hypothesis, or proposal is promoted into canonical State/Fact/Relation authority.

failure_families.name: False omission
failure_families.definition: A required current item, fact, relation, evidence source, or query facet is absent.

failure_families.name: Lifecycle corruption
failure_families.definition: A State/Fact/Relation has an illegal or outdated current status.

failure_families.name: Stale resurrection
failure_families.definition: Superseded, retracted, resolved, or outdated evidence is treated as current authority.

failure_families.name: Future leakage
failure_families.definition: Cutoff-after information affects a prefix, answer, classification, or packet.

failure_families.name: Duplicate confusion
failure_families.definition: Semantic repetition is overcounted as independent corroboration or independent evidence is collapsed.

failure_families.name: Scope transfer
failure_families.definition: A fact or rule is transferred to a similar but distinct person, site, object, or timeline.

failure_families.name: Contradiction mishandling
failure_families.definition: Conflicting evidence is flattened without authority, timing, or ambiguity handling.

failure_families.name: Relation corruption
failure_families.definition: Relation type, direction, endpoint, lifecycle, or dependency closure is wrong.

failure_families.name: Multi-facet incompleteness
failure_families.definition: An answer is locally correct but omits one or more required facets.

failure_families.name: Selective classification failure
failure_families.definition: The system answers when Gold requires abstention, or abstains when sufficient evidence exists.

failure_families.name: Provenance failure
failure_families.definition: A claim lacks required evidence, cites forbidden evidence, or misstates source independence.

failure_families.name: Long-range continuity failure
failure_families.definition: Old but still relevant evidence is lost after a large chapter/token gap.

failure_families.name: Unsupported addition
failure_families.definition: The answer invents a person, event, status, rationale, or relation not supported at cutoff.

failure_families.name: Surface traceability failure
failure_families.definition: A required event or semantic unit cannot be stably located in eligible corpus bytes, preventing layer-specific failure attribution.

case_families.name: Formation typing and selective promotion
case_families.description: Separate canonical Goal/Constraint/Decision/OpenQuestion/RejectedAlternative proposals from Fact, observation, and noise.
mechanical_checks: every target event has Gold delta
non-empty and true-negative denominators are non-zero
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Did the corpus make the intended type and authority distinguishable without exam-like labels?

case_families.name: Brainstorming versus formal Decision
case_families.description: A repeated proposal or brainstorming thread appears well before a separate formal adoption event.
mechanical_checks: Decision transition cannot precede formal event
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Could a fluent reader tell what was merely discussed and what was actually decided?

case_families.name: Typed State lifecycle
case_families.description: Exercise legal creation, update, terminal, and current-status transitions for every State type.
mechanical_checks: current status at cutoff is deterministic
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does prose express every lifecycle change and avoid implying unregistered changes?

case_families.name: Supersession chain
case_families.description: A current Decision, Constraint, Goal, Fact, or Relation is replaced while historical evidence remains.
mechanical_checks: old item is not current after cutoff
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is the old authority clearly historical rather than erased or still current?

case_families.name: Retraction without inverse invention
case_families.description: An authority retracts a claim, Decision, Constraint, or Relation without automatically proving the opposite.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does the text preserve uncertainty instead of implying the inverse after retraction?

case_families.name: Resolve and reopen
case_families.description: OpenQuestions resolve on evidence and some later reopen on new evidence without losing history.
mechanical_checks: reopen returns same scoped question to OPEN
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is tracker/meeting closure kept distinct from genuine semantic resolution?

case_families.name: RejectedAlternative continuity
case_families.description: Rejected alternatives remain historically visible and are not silently revived by recency or repetition.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does later discussion tempt a stale revival without actually authorizing it?

case_families.name: Fact and observation authority
case_families.description: Distinguish mutable world facts, firsthand observations, reports, hypotheses, and corrections.
mechanical_checks: fact transition distinguishes correction from world-state change
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Are observations neither overpromoted to certainty nor ignored when independently confirmed?

case_families.name: Semantic duplicate and source independence
case_families.description: Repeated wording is classified as same-source, derived, independent confirmation, or independent contradiction.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Would a reader mistakenly count copied reports as several independent sources?

case_families.name: Misleading and stage-error correction
case_families.description: Plausible but wrong interim information is later corrected or left unresolved.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is the error plausible without unfairly hiding the correction or telegraphing the answer?

case_families.name: Stale evidence
case_families.description: Previously reliable evidence becomes outdated by later state change, supersession, retraction, or scope change.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Can the answer acknowledge history without resurrecting it as current truth?

case_families.name: Long-range recall
case_families.description: An early anchor becomes necessary again after at least twelve chapters and substantial unrelated material.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is the old evidence genuinely necessary, not merely decorative or restated nearby?

case_families.name: Old-relevant versus recent-salient
case_families.description: Recent vivid material competes with older, less salient evidence that actually answers the query.
mechanical_checks: recent event is visible but forbidden or optional
old event belongs to required evidence set
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does recency create a fair distraction without making the old answer unknowable?

case_families.name: Negative-transfer sentinel
case_families.description: Highly similar entities, names, sites, or rules are explicitly distinct; evidence for one must not transfer to another.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is the similarity strong enough to test transfer while preserving a discoverable distinction?

case_families.name: Multi-facet completeness
case_families.description: One query requires facts and current State across two or more topics or timelines.
mechanical_checks: every required semantic unit belongs to a facet
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Can an answer be partly correct yet measurably incomplete without relying on style preferences?

case_families.name: Cross-chapter Fact join
case_families.description: A Fact answer requires joining non-redundant evidence from separated chapters.
mechanical_checks: required evidence spans at least two chapters
ALL_OF set has at least two events
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does each evidence fragment contribute a necessary piece rather than repeat the same claim?

case_families.name: Parallel timeline disambiguation
case_families.description: Several timelines advance concurrently and occasionally disclose older events out of calendar order.
mechanical_checks: both time axes are total where required
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does the reader have enough cues to distinguish when something happened from when it became known?

case_families.name: Ambiguity and ABSTAIN
case_families.description: Some cutoffs lack enough evidence, permit several answers, or support only qualified partial answers.
mechanical_checks: ambiguity mode and expected action are explicit
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Is abstention demanded by genuine evidence limits rather than vague wording?

case_families.name: Relation chain and endpoint integrity
case_families.description: Questions require following typed dependencies, supersession, resolution, provenance, or entity relations.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does the corpus express direction and dependency strongly enough to distinguish adjacent relations?

case_families.name: Query cutoff and future leakage
case_families.description: A later answer or correction exists but must remain invisible to an earlier query.
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Would the earlier prefix genuinely support only the registered pre-resolution answer?

case_families.name: Surface evidence traceability
case_families.description: Required events and semantic units have stable corpus byte identity and exact coordinates so omissions can be attributed to retrieval, formation, or answering.
mechanical_checks: all required event and semantic unit IDs map before relevant cutoff
no invalid generation attempt is mapped
case_families.semantic_audit_question: Does each mapped surface express the registered event or semantic unit rather than merely share vocabulary?
